To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
electrochemical dealloyed Pd-Ni alloy nanoporous metals can be used as enzyme-free electrochemical sensors for glucose detection.
we have developed a facile approach for the preparation of Pd-based nanoporous metals by dealloying Pd-containing Pd-Nic-P metallic glasses.

the Pd-NicP metallic glasses can be used as precursors for electrochemically dealloying palladinous nanoporous metals with tunable ligament and pore size, which exhibit enzyme-free electrochemical catalytic activities towards the oxidation of glucose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of enzyme-free electrocatalyst for the detection of d-glucose by dealloying metallic glasses.
the preparation of enzyme-free electrochemcial glucose sensors by dealloying Pd-based metallic glasses.
the formation of enzymeless glucose sensors by electrochemically dealloying palladious Pd-Ni metallic glasses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrochemical dealloyed Pd-Ni metallic glass is a promising material to fabricate the enzyme-free electrochemical sensor for the detection of d-glucose.
the nanoporous metal prepared by dealloy of Pd-Ni metallic glasses is a promising candidate for the electrochemical sensor of glucose.

the nanoporous metal obtained by dealloying Pd-rich Pd-Ni alloys has a higher electrocatalytic activity for the oxidation of dglucose, and the electrocatalytic performance can be further enhanced when the Pd-Niporous alloy is used as the precursor alloy for dealloying.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrochemical dealloyed Pd-Ni nanoporous metals with high Pd content are the most suitable materials to be used as the enzyme-free electrochemical sensor.

the dealloying process can be used as a general method to prepare nanoporous metals from Pd-based metallic glasses with different compositions, and these nanoporous metals can be used as electrochemical glucose sensors.

we can prepare nanoporous palladium-based metals with different ligaments and pores sizes, and the chemical compositions of the as-obtined nanoporous metals can also be tuned by varying the precursor alloy compositions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrochemical catalytic performance of the as-obtainted nanoporous metals is highly dependent on the ligament and pore size of the nanoporous structures.
the dealloying method can be used to prepare electrochemical sensors based on the electrochemical oxidation of glucose.
